note: Timor-Leste: the Migration Service's Temporary Stay Visa is for specialised activities, cultural and sporting among them, 'as an artist', at US$50 for the first application or an extension; the Working Visa (US$100, up to one year, renewable) is for employment or service contracts, with the employer's terms certified by SEFOPE. A performer's engagement is taken as the artist's specialised activity, so the Temporary Stay Visa is the route. The EU visa waiver excludes paid activity, and no days of work without a visa are named, so none are modelled. Read on the Migration Service's own pages (Law on Migration and Asylum).

sources.title: Migration Service of Timor-Leste, Temporary Stay Visa
sources.said: The temporary stay visa is intended for foreign nationals engaged in the following: ... Specialized activities, including cultural, sporting, scientific research, journalistic or highly qualified activities as an artist, sportsman, researcher, foreign media correspondent, or highly qualified technician; ... The fee for initial application and any extension is US$50, payable in cash at the time of application.

sources.title: Migration Service of Timor-Leste, Working Visa
sources.said: The work visa is intended to allow the holder to entry into the territory national in order to pursue an occupation for others, under the form of employment contract or service, including the volunteer who wishes to pursue volunteer activities for periods exceeding 120 days per year. The work visa is valid for a maximum period of one year, it may be extended for equal periods and allows multiple entries.
